source.quote: By virtue of the authority vested in me by the act of June 25, 1910, c. 421, 36 Stat. 847, Executive Orders No. 4109 of December 8, 1924, No. 4262 of July 3, 1925, and No. 4430 of April 23, 1926, withdrawing public lands in the States of Alabama, Florida, Mississippi, Michigan, and Wisconsin, are hereby revoked, the lands thus released becoming subject to the provisions of Executive Order No. 6964 of February 5, 1935, withdrawing public lands in the States herein mentioned and other States for classification and other purposes.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Whole withdrawal revoked by EO 8861 (Franklin D. Roosevelt, August 20, 1941): 'Executive Orders No. 4109 of December 8, 1924, No. 4262 of July 3, 1925, and No. 4430 of April 23, 1926 ... are hereby revoked'. EO 8861 states no effective date; recorded as effective on signing, 1941-08-20 (the alternative reading, effect on Federal Register publication at 6 FR 4289 on August 22, 1941, is disclosed). Earlier events each ended the withdrawal only for the lands they name: EO 4372 (1926-01-23, Batton Islands and Key Biscayne), EO 4485 (1926-07-24, part of Amelia Island); EO 7993 (1938-10-27, Great White Heron Refuge lands) and EO 8508 (1940-08-08, 195.26 acres in T. 3 S., R. 31 W.) did the same and are disclosed in the rationale. EO 8725 (1941-03-29) took precedence over EO 4109 for its gunnery-range lands but expressly did not rescind or revoke it, so it ended no part. Actor of the end: EO 8861.

source.quote:
it is hereby ordered that
Executive order of December 8, 1924, No. 4109, withdrawing certain islands in
Florida, belonging to the United States situated in the waters off the coast or in
the coastal waters of the State, be revoked in so far as it applies to the lands
included in the abandoned military reservation on Batton Islands in T. 1 S., Rs. 28
and 29 E., Tal. M., Florida, and those included in the abandoned" military reserva-
tion at Key Biscayne, in T. 54 S., R. 42 E., Tal. M., Florida, the disposal of which
is authorized by the act of July 5, 1884 (23 Stat., 103).

it ishereby ordered that Executive Order No. 4109, dated December 8, 1924, with-drawing all islands situate in the coastal waters of Florida belonging to the United.States, from settlement, location, sale, entry and all forms of appropriation subjectto valid existing rights in and to the same, pending classification and legislation, berevoked in so far as said order applies to- fractional Sec. 6, T. 1 N., R. 29 E., Tal.M., a portion of Amelia Island, situated in the coastal waters of Florida;' and saidtract is hereby restored to settlement and entry under appropriate public land laws.

The withdrawal made by this order 
shall take precedence over but shall not 
rescind or revoke as to any of the lands 
affected thereby in the above-described 
area, Executive Orders No. 4109 of De­
cember 8, 1924, No. 4262 of July 3, 1925, 
and No. 6964 of February 5, 1935, with­
drawing certain lands for classification 
and in aid of legislation.

research_rationale:
EO 4109 (December 8, 1924, Calvin Coolidge), read in full in the held ProQuest replica scan (archival_replica_scan_pending_codebook, acceptable_as_original false) and checked against the page image rendered from the held PDF (ProQuest Pre-1937 Orders/PT1-1924-EO-4109.pdf, sha256 e75a8313...; one page; heading 'Executive Order', 'FLORIDA', signature 'CALVIN COOLIDGE', 'The White House, December 8, 1924', '[No. 4109]'; Interior received stamp December 18, 1924; State Department true-copy date December 17, 1924). The OCR layer holds every printed line of the order; its errors ('Executve odber', 'the. same', stamp noise) do not touch the operative words. One operative command: under the act of June 25, 1910 (36 Stat. 847) as amended August 24, 1912 (37 Stat. 497), 'all islands belonging to the United States in Florida situated in the waters off the coast or in the coastal waters of the State' are withdrawn from settlement, location, sale, entry and all forms of appropriation, subject to valid existing rights, 'for classification and in aid of legislation'. No stated effective date; effective on signing. The order states no term and no own-terms end: its purpose (classification and legislation) is not shown to have been completed, and completion would not itself have ended a withdrawal that runs until revoked. First and whole end: EO 8861 (Franklin D. Roosevelt, August 20, 1941), held as an APP mirror transcription (page record checked: MIRROR_DOCUMENTS row heading names EO 8861 and Nos. 4109, 4262 and 4430, date 1941-08-20, text_sha256 equals the held text) and in the held Federal Register text of 6 FR 4289 (August 22, 1941; F.R. Doc. 41-6244, filed August 21, 1941): the three orders 'are hereby revoked, the lands thus released becoming subject to the provisions of Executive Order No. 6964 of February 5, 1935'. EO 8861 states no effective date; recorded as 1941-08-20, the signing date, with publication on August 22, 1941 as the disclosed alternative. Partial later events cited: EO 4372 (January 23, 1926; ProQuest scan, page image checked) revoked EO 4109 as to the abandoned military reservations on Batton Islands and Key Biscayne; EO 4485 (July 24, 1926; ProQuest scan, page image checked) as to fractional sec. 6, T. 1 N., R. 29 E., on Amelia Island; EO 8725 (March 29, 1941; aerial gunnery ranges; held Federal Register text) 'shall take precedence over but shall not rescind or revoke' EO 4109 for its lands, recorded as a later event that ended nothing. Two further partial events are held but disclosed rather than cited, because the dossier offers them only as APP transcriptions while official Federal Register copies are held (jobs/fr-originals/output/texts/EO_7993.txt and EO_8508.txt) and the working-text gate refuses a transcription when an official copy exists: EO 7993 (October 27, 1938; Great White Heron Refuge) superseded EO 4109 'insofar as such withdrawals affect the above-described lands', and EO 8508 (August 8, 1940; antiaircraft firing range, 195.26 acres in T. 3 S., R. 31 W.) superseded it 'as to any of the above-described lands'. Each released only named lands before the whole revocation, so neither changes the first end or the status. The 1989 OFR codification disposition table (held: jobs/ofr-codification-1989/output/DISPOSITION_1989.csv) lists EO 4109 as 'Amended by EOs 4372, 4485, 7993, 8508' and 'Revoked by EO 8861', which matches this inventory of events. Contrary evidence checked: the dossier's actor records for EOs 8858, 8859 and 8860 come from the same Federal Register pages (6 FR 4288-4289) as EO 8861 and are page-neighbour artefacts; the held FR texts of EOs 7994, 8509, 8510 and 8724 that mention EO 4109 are the same pages as EOs 7993, 8508 and 8725; a citation search of every held order text found no instrument after August 20, 1941 that names EO 4109.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"No earlier whole end. The four earlier events (EOs 4372, 4485, 7993, 8508) each name the lands they release or reserve, and the withdrawal continued for all other Florida islands. EO 6964 (February 5, 1935), the general withdrawal of public lands in the eastern states, overlapped EO 4109 without revoking it (EOs 7993, 8508 and 8861 all treat EO 4109 as still operating afterwards). No statute naming EO 4109 is held or found.","independent_command_check":"No independent command. The citation of the 1910 act and its 1912 amendment is authority; 'subject to any valid existing rights' is an exception to the withdrawal, not a separate command.","savings_check":"EO 8861 contains no savings clause. The lands it released became 'subject to the provisions of Executive Order No. 6964 of February 5, 1935'; that continuing withdrawal is EO 6964's own command and belongs to its lifecycle, not a residual of EO 4109. Valid existing rights were excepted from the withdrawal from the start and were never affected by it. Lands reserved by EOs 7993 and 8508 continued under those orders, not under EO 4109.","scope_check":"Whole order is one clause, one withdrawal of one class of land (Florida islands). Partial events are recorded as later events; the whole clause ended with EO 8861."}

savings_residuals.reason: EO 8861 contains no savings clause. The lands it released became 'subject to the provisions of Executive Order No. 6964 of February 5, 1935'; that continuing withdrawal is EO 6964's own command and belongs to its lifecycle, not a residual of EO 4109. Valid existing rights were excepted from the withdrawal from the start and were never affected by it. Lands reserved by EOs 7993 and 8508 continued under those orders, not under EO 4109.

research_rationale:
EO 4430 (April 23, 1926, Calvin Coolidge), read in full in the held ProQuest replica scan (archival_replica_scan_pending_codebook, acceptable_as_original false) and checked against the page image rendered from the held PDF (ProQuest Pre-1937 Orders/PT1-1926-EO-4430.pdf, sha256 f52572ba...; one page; 'Executive Order', 'Michigan and Wisconsin', 'CALVIN COOLIDGE', 'The White House, April 23, 1926', '[No. 4430]'; Interior received stamp May 3, 1926; State Department true copy May 1, 1926; a handwritten note '8861 - 8/20/41 ... Fed Reg 8/22/41'). The OCR layer holds every printed line; it misreads the date as 'April 28' (the image reads April 23, as do EO 8861, EO 4446 and EO 7814) and garbles words such as 'Pursudhit' and 'rigIts' without changing the operative content. One operative command: under the act of June 25, 1910 as amended August 24, 1912, and with the exception of lands whose disposal is authorized by the act of July 5, 1884, all public lands 'bordering on meandered lakes and all islands therein in the States of Michigan and Wisconsin, and all lands within three miles of the shore of Lakes Michigan, Huron or Superior, in said States, and all islands within the lakes last mentioned' are withdrawn from settlement, location, sale, entry and all forms of appropriation, subject to valid existing rights, pending classification and legislation. No stated effective date; effective on signing; no stated term. First and whole end: EO 8861 (August 20, 1941), held as an APP mirror transcription (page record checked: heading names EO 8861 and No. 4430, date 1941-08-20, text_sha256 equals the held text) and in the held Federal Register text of 6 FR 4289 (August 22, 1941): 'Executive Orders No. 4109 of December 8, 1924, No. 4262 of July 3, 1925, and No. 4430 of April 23, 1926 ... are hereby revoked, the lands thus released becoming subject to the provisions of Executive Order No. 6964'. Recorded as 1941-08-20 (signing); publication on August 22, 1941 is the disclosed alternative. Partial later event cited: EO 4446 (May 21, 1926; ProQuest scan, page image checked), revoking EO 4430 as to Wisconsin lands whose disposal the act of February 27, 1925 authorizes. Further partial events are disclosed but not cited; each ended the withdrawal only for named lands before the whole revocation, so none changes the first end or the status: EO 7795 (January 21, 1938; Huron Migratory Bird Refuge), whose reservation 'supersedes as to any of the above-described islands affected thereby the temporary withdrawal ... made by Executive Order No. 4430', and EO 7814 (February 15, 1938; lot 1, sec. 9, T. 32 N., R. 9 W., Fourth Principal Meridian, Wisconsin), both held as APP transcriptions (page records checked) and as official Federal Register texts (jobs/fr-originals/output/texts/EO_7795.txt, EO_7814.txt) that the dossier does not offer as citable alternatives (its Federal Register record for EO 7795 is sliced from the contents page, not the order), so the working-text gate refuses the transcriptions; EO 5366 (June 13, 1930, 160 acres in T. 27 N., R. 15 W., Michigan, for a homestead application) and EO 5386 (June 30, 1930, lands selected by Michigan under the act of July 31, 1912) are held as APP transcriptions but their supplement excerpts came out ungraded because the fragment registry holds two registrations of the same text (live and mirror), so the assembler cannot cite them; a partial revocation of EO 4430 'in so far as it affects any of the above-described lands' (with revocation of the lighthouse withdrawals of July 21 and October 20, 1874) is printed at 3 FR 2800 (Federal Register of November 30, 1938) beside Proclamation 2313 of November 25, 1938 in the held text jobs/fr-originals/output/texts/EO_8014.txt, but its acting instrument cannot be fixed from the column-mixed OCR without the page image; Proclamation 2318, listed in the 1989 OFR codification disposition table (held: jobs/ofr-codification-1989/output/DISPOSITION_1989.csv) as amending EO 4430, is not held. That table lists EO 4430 as 'Amended by Procs. 2313, 2318; EOs 4446, 5366, 5386, 7795, 7814' and 'Revoked by EO 8861'. Contrary evidence checked: the dossier records for EO 7794 and the dossier's missing-provision pointers to EOs 7796, 7815 and 8014 are Federal Register page-neighbour artefacts (EO 7796 concerns state offices, EO 7815 West Point positions, EO 8014 Alaska military reservations); EOs 8858-8860 likewise share 6 FR 4288-4289 with EO 8861. A citation search of every held order text found no instrument after August 20, 1941 naming EO 4430.
